commands.name: flowleap:patstat-guarded-sql (MCP)
commands.description: Answer an aggregate patent question with agent-written SQL through `patstat_query` (CLI: `flowleap patstat query "<sql>" --question "<question>"`) under the deterministic gate — the one-retry loop. You own the retry: errors carry the exact parser/Postgres detail, fix once, never loop (the 10/min budget is the bound).

commands.name: flowleap:patstat-graph (MCP)
commands.description: Answer "named node and its relationships" questions — citations, family, applicants/inventors, or the path between two patents — with the resolve-first flow: resolve free-form input to an anchor/psn_id once with `patstat_resolve` (CLI: `flowleap patstat graph resolve <input>`), then call the graph tool that matches the question.

Perovskite tandem filings sit almost entirely in the H10K organic-device subclass, with the silicon bottom cell pulling in H10F. Two data sources agree: a Google Patents slice (July 2026) at subclass level, and PATSTAT 2026 Spring at subgroup level over 85 families whose title contains both "perovskite" and "tandem".

**Subclass level** (Google Patents, title or abstract contains "perovskite tandem"):

| Subclass | Meaning | Publications |
|---|---|---|
| H10K | Organic electric solid-state devices | 480 |
| H10F | Inorganic light-sensitive semiconductor devices | 112 |
| Y02E | Greenhouse-gas reduction tag, energy generation | 66 |
| H01G | Electrolytic capacitors and photoelectrochemical devices | 24 |
| H01L | Legacy semiconductor subclass, pre-reclassification | 18 |

**Subgroup level** (PATSTAT, 85 families, ranked by families):

- **H10K85/50** Organic and hybrid organic-inorganic perovskites, the material code. 47 families.
- **H10K30/57** Organic PV comprising multiple junctions, e.g. tandem cells. 46 families. This is the most discriminating code for the concept.
- **H10K30/40** p-i-n structure with a perovskite absorber between charge transport layers. 30 families.
- **H10K39/15** Assemblies comprising both organic and inorganic PV cells. 24 families. This is where perovskite-on-silicon lands.
- **H10F10/19** Inorganic PV cells with multiple potential barriers of different types, e.g. tandem cells. 19 families.
- **H10K30/10** Heterojunctions between organic and inorganic semiconductors. 19 families.
- **H10F10/161** and **H10F10/142** Multiple PN heterojunctions or homojunctions, tandem cells. 12 and 8 families.
- **H01G9/2072** Photoelectrochemical devices with two or more photoelectrodes for different spectral ranges. 4 families, the dye-sensitised legacy route.

**Tag codes to ignore for landscaping.** Y02E10/549 "Organic PV cells" is the single most frequent code at 59 families, but it is a climate tag applied to nearly every organic PV filing. Y02P70/50 and Y02E10/544 and Y02E10/548 behave the same way.

**Practical search set.** For a corpus definition, use H10K30/57 OR H10K39/15, optionally AND H10K85/50 to exclude non-perovskite organic tandems. Add H10F10/19 and H10F10/161 to catch filings classified from the silicon side. Older filings may still carry H01L31 and H01L51 codes in other databases, since the H10F and H10K subclasses only replaced them in 2023 and 2025; the PATSTAT edition used here has already been reclassified.

One caveat on the seed. Both corpora are title or abstract matches, so filings that say "multijunction" or "perovskite/silicon" without the word "tandem" are missed. The perovskite-silicon phrase variant on Google Patents produced the same top codes, which supports the ranking.

**Subgroup level** (PATSTAT, 85 families, ranked by families):

- **H10K85/50** Organic and hybrid organic-inorganic perovskites, the material code. 47 families.
- **H10K30/57** Organic PV comprising multiple junctions, e.g. tandem cells. 46 families. This is the most discriminating code for the concept.
- **H10K30/40** p-i-n structure with a perovskite absorber between charge transport layers. 30 families.
- **H10K39/15** Assemblies comprising both organic and inorganic PV cells. 24 families. This is where perovskite-on-silicon lands.
- **H10F10/19** Inorganic PV cells with multiple potential barriers of different types, e.g. tandem cells. 19 families.
- **H10K30/10** Heterojunctions between organic and inorganic semiconductors. 19 families.
- **H10F10/161** and **H10F10/142** Multiple PN heterojunctions or homojunctions, tandem cells. 12 and 8 families.
- **H01G9/2072** Photoelectrochemical devices with two or more photoelectrodes for different spectral ranges. 4 families, the dye-sensitised legacy route.

**Tag codes to ignore for landscaping.** Y02E10/549 "Organic PV cells" is the single most frequent code at 59 families, but it is a climate tag applied to nearly every organic PV filing. Y02P70/50 and Y02E10/544 and Y02E10/548 behave the same way.

**Practical search set.** For a corpus definition, use H10K30/57 OR H10K39/15, optionally AND H10K85/50 to exclude non-perovskite organic tandems. Add H10F10/19 and H10F10/161 to catch filings classified from the silicon side. Older filings may still carry H01L31 and H01L51 codes in other databases, since the H10F and H10K subclasses only replaced them in 2023 and 2025; the PATSTAT edition used here has already been reclassified.

One caveat on the seed. Both corpora are title or abstract matches, so filings that say "multijunction" or "perovskite/silicon" without the word "tandem" are missed. The perovskite-silicon phrase variant on Google Patents produced the same top codes, which supports the ranking.
